newsitem.title: Austria: ALPINE SKIING-REITER WINS CLASSIC KITZBUEHEL SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-REITER WINS CLASSIC KITZBUEHEL SLALOM.

text.p: Austria's Mario Reiter captured his first victory of the World Cup season at the classic men's slalom in Kitzbuehel on Sunday, ahead of Italian Alberto Tomba.
Reiter, the 1996 world championship slalom silver medallist, clocked a winning aggregate time of one minute 36.09 seconds on the Ganslern piste, for his third career World Cup win.
"I didn't think I could do it today. Winning Kitzbuehel has always been my dream. I am not going to ski for much longer so it's good that I fulfilled one of my goals already," said Reiter.

Reiter's victory came as a surprise as the 26-year-old Austrian had a weak start to the season following health problems. He won his only other slalom in 1996 in Sestriere, site of this year's world championships which open next Sunday.
Tomba produced a wild but fast second run to improve on a first-leg fifth place for overall second in 1:36.28, to demonstrate that he is in good form for Sestriere despite recent injury and illness.
The Italian world and former Olympic champion had completed only two of this season's slaloms before Sunday after wrist and knee injuries were followed by a bout of influenza.
Norway's Finn Christian Jagge, the 1992 Olympic slalom champion, made his first appearance on the podium this season with third place in 1:36.54.

In-form Austrian Thomas Sykora, who was suffering from hip pains after a fall in Sunday morning's free practice, disappointed in the second run and fell back from first place after the opening run to overall seventh.
Last year's winner here, Sykora has won five of the seven slaloms staged so far this season and finished second once to put him well ahead in the discipline standings.
It was the first time in a year that Sykora had failed to finish on the slalom World Cup rostrum.
Defending overall World Cup champion Lasse Kjus of Norway won the combined event which twinned Sunday's slalom with Saturday's downhill here.
His team mate Kjetil Andre Aamodt was second in the combined with Austrian Werner Franz third.
